memos.headline: S08 and S09 Lead at 52-Week Highs; S07 in Freefall With RSI Near 30
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. S08 and S09 are both sitting at their 52-week highs with strong relative strength versus SPY, though S09's RSI of 73 and +9.3% extension above its 50-day mean warn of a near-term pullback risk. S04 has been the standout performer over 12 weeks (+38.6%) with relative strength of +35.3% vs SPY, yet its RSI at 57 and only -2.6% drawdown suggest the trend still has room. On the weak side, S07 is in a confirmed downtrend—down 31.4% from its high, 10.1% below its 50-day mean, RSI at 30.7, and losing nearly 22% relative to SPY over 12 weeks—this is a name to avoid until price reclaims its 200-day average. S05 concerns me with a 15.4% drawdown and price essentially flat to its 200-day mean, suggesting the intermediate trend is breaking down.

views.note: At 52-week high with RSI 62, well above both moving averages, and positive relative strength; I'd reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~326).
Massive 12-week momentum of +38.6% with RSI still only 57 and relative strength of +35% vs SPY; would cut on a break below 505 (~4.5% lower).
At 52-week high with best 4-week relative strength in the universe (+9.2%), but RSI 73 and +9.3% above 50-day mean make chasing risky; a pullback to the 50-day (~164) would be a better entry.
Strong recent momentum with +8.9% over 4 weeks and positive relative strength, but RSI 75.2 is the most overbought in the universe and a mean-reversion is likely near-term.
Confirmed downtrend: -31.4% drawdown, RSI 30.7, 10% below 50-day and 9% below 200-day, worst relative strength in the group; no buy until price reclaims the 200-day (~805).
Price flat to 200-day mean, -15.4% drawdown, RSI 44 and negative relative strength over 4 weeks; trend is deteriorating and I'd need a reclaim above 350 to reconsider.
RSI 37.5 with -6.6% weekly loss and -4% below 50-day mean; relative strength turning negative and 10.5% off highs signals distribution.
RSI 51 is neutral but -6.3% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks and -2.8% over 4 weeks show persistent underperformance; no edge either way until it breaks above 365 or below 320.
Strong 1-week bounce of +5.8% and positive 4-week relative strength, but still -8% off highs and -5.2% over 12 weeks; this looks like a counter-trend rally within a choppy range.
RSI 45 and -12% drawdown with weakening 4-week relative strength; sitting in no-man's land between the 50-day and 200-day, need a decisive move above 260 to get constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 and S01 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, expanding earnings power and those suffering margin erosion. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth, a 62% net margin, and $59.7B in net income on only $33.4B of total debt—this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 is similarly exceptional: 93.7% net margin, 24% revenue growth, near-zero leverage at $14.8B debt, and net income up 298% YoY. On the other end, S09 posted just 4.9% net margin with net income down 46% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth, and S01 saw net income decline 16% YoY with revenue barely growing at 1.5%. I would need to see S09 stabilize margins above 7% and S01 return to double-digit earnings growth before reconsidering either name. S03's 245% net income growth on 20% revenue growth is impressive but I want to see whether that margin expansion is sustainable given $133B in total debt.

views.note: 106% revenue growth, 62% net margin, and modest $33.4B debt make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
93.7% net margin with minimal leverage ($14.8B debt) and 298% YoY net income growth reflects extraordinary earnings power.
39.7% net margin, 18% revenue growth, and 31% earnings growth with manageable $40.3B debt support a durable compounder thesis.
245% net income growth is compelling but $133B total debt and the question of margin sustainability temper my conviction.
24% revenue growth and 65% earnings growth with a 17.5% net margin show solid operating leverage, though $36.2B debt on $20.5B revenue warrants monitoring.
Strong 28% revenue growth and 37% margin are offset by $460.5B in total debt, which dominates the balance sheet.
16% revenue growth and 27% margin are solid but $82.3B debt and decelerating growth relative to peers keep me on the sideline.
Revenue essentially flat at +0.4% YoY with a thin 4.9% net margin; 61% earnings recovery helps but I need to see top-line acceleration.
Net income down 46% YoY on 2.4% revenue growth with a 4.9% margin signals clear earnings deterioration.
Revenue growth of just 1.5% and a 16% decline in net income point to fading earnings power; need to see margin stabilization above 15%.

memos.headline: Sticky 3.7% YoY CPI and 5.09% 10y Yield Signal a Hawkish Pause Regime — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a clear hawkish-pause regime: the Fed has actually raised the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, CPI is running at 3.7% YoY with the index up 1.1% in just the last three months, and the 10y yield has surged 110bp over the past year to 5.09%. The labor market remains firm at 4.2% unemployment, unchanged over three months and down 20bp YoY, giving the Fed no urgency to ease. The 10y-2y spread has flattened 22bp over the past year to just +33bp, consistent with the market pricing a prolonged restrictive stance. This environment is punishing for long-duration growth equities and supportive for banks earning wider net interest margins, while staples should hold up as a defensive allocation. A CPI print that decelerates below 3.0% YoY or unemployment rising above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward easing and favor duration.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth faces severe headwinds with the 10y at 5.09% and no easing in sight given sticky 3.7% CPI.
Banks benefit from a hawkish-pause regime with elevated short rates at 4.00% and a positively sloped curve supporting net interest margins.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a restrictive-rate environment with firm labor markets keeping consumer spending resilient.
Cyclicals face margin pressure as the hawkish pause tightens financial conditions; the 52bp rise in the 10y over three months is a headwind.
Energy is mixed — firm labor supports demand but rising real rates and a flattening curve limit upside; I lack conviction here.
With the 10y yield at 5.09% and CPI still at 3.7% YoY, rate-sensitive sectors face continued multiple compression.

memos.headline: S10 Post-Earnings Momentum Fading; S07 Leadership Churn Warrants Caution
memos.body: I am reviewing the 8-K filing cadence and associated price reactions across the universe as of today. S10 posted an impressive +8.7% move on its late-August earnings release, but with no further positive catalysts since a routine 'Other Events' filing on Sep 3, I suspect the positive sentiment is largely priced. S06 and S02 both reported results on Oct 13 with muted-to-slightly-negative price reactions (-0.9% and -0.2% respectively), suggesting the market had already discounted their narratives. S07 stands out with a new material debt obligation filed Sep 1 followed by a leadership change just yesterday (Oct 15), a combination that often signals internal stress and could shift tone negatively if media picks up the story. I have limited conviction on names like S04 and S01 where only Reg FD disclosures have surfaced with no observable price signal.

views.note: The +8.7% earnings pop in late August is likely fully priced after seven weeks with no incremental positive catalysts.
New debt obligation combined with a leadership departure filed just yesterday raises the risk of a negative narrative shift.
Earnings and Reg FD disclosures on Oct 13 drew only a -0.9% reaction, suggesting sentiment is flat and already absorbed.
Oct 13 earnings produced a negligible -0.2% move, indicating the market sees no new information worth repricing.
A director/officer change via 8-K/A in early September is stale news with no follow-up filings to shift tone.
Two September filings including a leadership change and an 'Other Events' disclosure have had over a month to be digested with no visible sentiment shift.

memos.headline: Oil at $105 and Widening HY Spreads Signal Geopolitical Supply Risk Despite Falling Policy Uncertainty
memos.body: I see a divergent macro picture: WTI crude has surged nearly 30% over three months to $104.71/bbl, pointing to a meaningful supply disruption or geopolitical energy-security event, even as the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed 57% over the same period to 125.69. The HY OAS widening of +52bp over three months to 3.23% tells me credit markets are pricing some stress that equity vol (VIX at 16.46) is not fully reflecting. I interpret the oil spike as a structural supply-side tightening—possibly sanctions enforcement or OPEC+ discipline—rather than a demand-driven move, given the flattening yield curve (10y-2y at 0.33pp, down 9bp over 3 months). My conviction is highest on energy-exposed names benefiting from elevated crude and lowest on credit-sensitive industrials facing margin compression; a reversal in oil below $90 or new sanctions relief would change my view materially.

views.note: No company-specific filings to anchor a directional view; macro backdrop is mixed with falling uncertainty but rising credit spreads.
Recent 8-K (Other Events) lacks detail, and without clarity on supply-chain or sanctions exposure I stay sidelined despite the oil-driven macro shift.
Reg FD disclosure filed mid-October alongside a 30% crude rally suggests potential energy-sector tailwind; elevated oil prices structurally favor upstream or energy-linked names.

HY OAS widening of 52bp over three months raises refinancing and margin risk for credit-sensitive names; Reg FD filing in early September predates the oil spike and may not reflect current cost pressures.
Recent Reg FD disclosure is noted but without content detail; falling policy uncertainty is a mild positive, though oil-driven input cost risk keeps me from going long.
8-K filed just yesterday (Oct 15) during a period of sharply falling policy uncertainty and stabilizing VIX suggests proactive corporate positioning; I lean constructive pending content clarity.
Early-September 8-K predates the 30% oil surge; names with high energy-input sensitivity face margin headwinds unless they can pass through costs.

We keep ~40% cash given macro headwinds and elevated uncertainty in credit markets.

Geopolitics analyst's HY spread concern is noted but S04's strong balance sheet ($40.3B debt) mitigates refinancing risk.
